screen.name: Screen
screen.note: Its cable plugs into J1. The screen's own pin names: GND, IO27, IO28, 5V on the Gen 3.5 (ESP32-P4); GND, IO18, IO17, 5V on the Gen 3 (ESP32-S3); GND, RX, TX, 5V on the headless board. J1's TX goes to the first of the middle two, its RX to the second.

F2.what: Neutral from the inlet to the power switch

F4.what: Earth from the cup warmer to the chassis

F5.what: Earth from the chassis to the 3-way valve

F6.what: Earth from the 3-way valve to the boiler

F7.what: Switched line from the power switch

F8.what: Power lamp lead, on the switched line

F9.what: Switched line to the 184 °C thermal fuse

F11.what: Line to the brew switch, which feeds the pump and valve

F14.what: Switched neutral from the power switch

F15.what: The pump's return: its 110 °C fuse's lead (the fuse's other lead is Pa, on the pump)

F16.what: Neutral on to the power and brew lamps, the brew thermostat and the steam switch

F19.what: Neutral to the brew thermostat: the heater's return

F21.what: Jumper on the steam switch: steam on joins the thermostats' midpoint to neutral, bypassing the brew thermostat

F22.what: The 3-way valve's return, through the steam switch, so it only opens with steam off

F23.what: The steam switch's bypass of the brew thermostat

F24.what: Brew lamp lead: across the brew thermostat, so it lights once that opens

F25.what: Steam lamp lead: across the steam thermostat

F26.what: Steam thermostat to the brew thermostat

F27.what: Brew thermostat to the steam thermostat

F28.what: Steam lamp lead, on the elements' return

F29.what: The elements' return to the steam thermostat

lampS.name: Steam lamp
lampS.note: Across the steam thermostat, so it lights once the boiler reaches steam temperature.

swS.name: Steam switch
swS.note: Steam off, it completes the 3-way valve's return to neutral. Steam on, it bypasses the brew thermostat, so the boiler heats to the steam thermostat's setting.

lampB.name: Brew lamp
lampB.note: Across the brew thermostat, so it lights once the boiler reaches brew temperature.

swB.name: Brew switch
swB.note: It joins line from after the thermal fuse (spade 4) to the 3-way valve's feed (spade 5), which also feeds the pump.

lampP.name: Power lamp
lampP.note: Between switched line and neutral, so it lights while the machine is on.

swP.name: Power switch
swP.note: It breaks both line (spades 4 and 5) and neutral (spades 1 and 2).

chassis.name: Chassis ground
chassis.note: Two earth spades on the frame.

cup.name: Cup warmer ground
cup.note: The cup warmer plate's earth spades.

boiler.name: Boiler
boiler.note: Two elements in parallel, with the 184 °C thermal fuse in series.

bt.name: Brew thermostat
bt.note: Out on every Gaggiuino install: the thermocouple goes in its hole, and the PCB takes over brew temperature.

st.name: Steam thermostat
st.note: On stock wiring it can stay, unplugged, or come out. On Plug-and-Play wiring the 185 °C resettable fuse goes in its hole.

sol.name: 3-way solenoid valve
sol.note: The 3-way solenoid valve. It opens while the brew switch is on with steam off.

sock.name: Power socket
sock.note: The IEC inlet: line, neutral and earth come in here.

pump.name: Pump and its 110 °C fuse
pump.note: The fuse's own lead plugs onto spade B (Pa, from its fuse). Its other lead runs to factory splice J0.

J0.name: Factory splice: neutral from the power switch, with the pump's return

J1.name: Factory splice: switched line from the power switch

J2.name: Factory splice: the neutral that feeds the power and brew lamps, the brew thermostat and the steam switch

J3.name: Factory splice: line after the 184 °C fuse

J4.name: Factory splice: between the two thermostats

J5.name: Factory splice: the elements' return to the steam thermostat

screen.name: Screen
screen.note: Its cable plugs into J1. The screen's own pin names: GND, IO27, IO28, 5V on the Gen 3.5 (ESP32-P4); GND, IO18, IO17, 5V on the Gen 3 (ESP32-S3); GND, RX, TX, 5V on the headless board. J1's TX goes to the first of the middle two, its RX to the second.

F1.what: Line from the inlet to the power switch

F2.what: Neutral from the inlet to the 184 °C thermal fuse

F3.what: Neutral after the thermal fuse, to an element

F4.what: Neutral to the pump, through its 110 °C fuse: this end is connector F

F5.what: Neutral on from connector F to the 3-way valve

F6.what: Neutral on to the power switch's spade 8, a tie point (the power lamp sits between P and 8)

F8.what: Switched line to the steam switch

F9.what: Switched line to the brew switch's common

F10.what: Switched line on to the brew thermostat

F11.what: Steam on joins spade 3 to P(3-4), so line skips the brew thermostat

F12.what: Brew thermostat to the steam thermostat

F13.what: Heater line from the steam thermostat to the brew switch's spade 2, a tie point (the boiler lamp sits between P and 2)

F14.what: Heater line on to an element

F15.what: Heater line to the other element

F16.what: Brew switch output to the steam switch's second pole, P(5-6)

F18.what: The 3-way valve's feed, through the steam switch, so it only opens with steam off

lampB.name: Internal boiler lamp
lampB.note: Inside the switch housing, wired across brew P(1-2) and 2 (dotted on the drawing). It lights once the boiler is up to temperature.

housing.name: Switch housing
housing.note: Brew, steam and power rockers in one block, with the boiler lamp inside across brew P(1-2) and 2, and the power lamp across on/off P and 8.

lampP.name: Internal power lamp
lampP.note: Inside the switch housing, wired across on/off P and 8 (dotted on the drawing). It lights while the machine is on.

cup.name: Cup warmer ground
cup.note: The cup warmer plate's earth spades. Most 120 V Classics left the factory with no earth wire, so none lands here: the grounding retrofit adds one.

boiler.name: Boiler
boiler.note: Two elements in parallel, with the 184 °C thermal fuse in series.

bt.name: Brew thermostat
bt.note: Out on every Gaggiuino install: the thermocouple goes in its hole, and the PCB takes over brew temperature.

st.name: Steam thermostat
st.note: On stock wiring it can stay, unplugged, or come out. On Plug-and-Play wiring the 185 °C resettable fuse goes in its hole.

sol.name: 3-way solenoid valve
sol.note: The 3-way solenoid valve. It opens while the brew switch is on with steam off.

sock.name: Power socket
sock.note: The IEC inlet. Most 120 V Classics have a two-pole one with no earth pin, so only line and neutral come in.

pump.name: Pump and its 110 °C fuse
pump.note: The fuse's own lead plugs onto spade B (Pa, from its fuse). Its other lead ends in connector F, which joins two wires.

fac.name: Classic, 120 V, as it leaves the factory
fac.srcname: the official docs' 120 V Classic stock-integration drawing, whose thick lines are the stock wires apart from the install's purple ones and the retrofit's green earth
fac.noearth: Most 120 V Classics left the factory with no earth wire, so none is drawn. The drawing's green earth wires are the grounding retrofit.

screen.name: Screen
screen.note: Its cable plugs into J1. The screen's own pin names: GND, IO27, IO28, 5V on the Gen 3.5 (ESP32-P4); GND, IO18, IO17, 5V on the Gen 3 (ESP32-S3); GND, RX, TX, 5V on the headless board. J1's TX goes to the first of the middle two, its RX to the second.

F1.what: Line from the inlet to the power switch

F2.what: Neutral from the inlet to the 184 °C thermal fuse

F3.what: Earth from the inlet to the boiler

F4.what: Earth from the boiler to the cup warmer

F5.what: Neutral after the thermal fuse, to the elements

F6.what: Neutral to the pump: this end is connector F

F7.what: Link between the two elements: at 230 V they run in series

F8.what: Heater line from the steam thermostat to the elements

F9.what: Heater line to the brew switch's spade 2, for the boiler lamp, which sits between P and 2

F10.what: Steam on joins spade 3 to P(3-4), so line skips the brew thermostat

F11.what: Brew thermostat to the steam thermostat

F12.what: Switched line to the brew thermostat

F13.what: Switched line to the steam switch

F14.what: Switched line on to the brew switch's common

F15.what: Brew switch output to the steam switch's second pole, P(5-6)

F17.what: The 3-way valve's feed, through the steam switch, so it only opens with steam off

F18.what: Neutral for the power lamp, which sits between P and 8: it reaches spade 8 from the 3-way valve's spade

F19.what: Neutral from the 3-way valve to connector F on the pump

lampB.name: Internal boiler lamp
lampB.note: Inside the switch housing, wired across brew P(1-2) and 2 (dotted on the drawing). It lights once the boiler is up to temperature.

housing.name: Switch housing
housing.note: Brew, steam and power rockers in one block, with the boiler lamp inside across brew P(1-2) and 2, and the power lamp across on/off P and 8.

lampP.name: Internal power lamp
lampP.note: Inside the switch housing, wired across on/off P and 8 (dotted on the drawing). It lights while the machine is on.

cup.name: Cup warmer ground
cup.note: The cup warmer plate's earth spades.

boiler.name: Boiler
boiler.note: Two elements in series, linked TL to BL, with the 184 °C thermal fuse in series.

bt.name: Brew thermostat
bt.note: Out on every Gaggiuino install: the thermocouple goes in its hole, and the PCB takes over brew temperature.

st.name: Steam thermostat
st.note: On stock wiring it can stay, unplugged, or come out. On Plug-and-Play wiring the 185 °C resettable fuse goes in its hole.

sol.name: 3-way solenoid valve
sol.note: The 3-way solenoid valve. It opens while the brew switch is on with steam off.

sock.name: Power socket
sock.note: The IEC inlet: line, neutral and earth come in here.

pump.name: Pump (no fuse on this drawing)
pump.note: This drawing shows no pump fuse. Connector F, on spade B, joins two neutral wires.

fac.name: Classic, 230 V, as it leaves the factory
fac.srcname: the official docs' 220 to 240 V Classic stock-integration drawing, whose thick lines are the stock wires apart from the install's purple ones

screen.note: Its cable plugs into J1. The screen's own pin names: GND, IO27, IO28, 5V on the Gen 3.5 (ESP32-P4); GND, IO18, IO17, 5V on the Gen 3 (ESP32-S3); GND, RX, TX, 5V on the headless board. J1's TX goes to the first of the middle two, its RX to the second.

F1.what: Line from the inlet to the power switch

F2.what: Neutral from the inlet to the power switch

F3.what: Earth from the inlet to the cup warmer

F4.what: Earth from the cup warmer to the chassis

F5.what: Earth from the chassis to the 3-way valve

F6.what: Earth from the 3-way valve to the boiler

F7.what: Switched line from the power switch

F8.what: Power lamp lead, on the switched line

F9.what: Switched line to the 184 °C thermal fuse

F11.what: Line to the brew switch, which feeds the pump and valve

F14.what: Switched neutral from the power switch

F15.what: The pump's return: its 110 °C fuse's lead (the fuse's other lead is Pa, on the pump)

F16.what: Neutral on to the power and brew lamps, the brew thermostat and the steam switch

F19.what: Neutral to the brew thermostat: the heater's return

F21.what: Jumper on the steam switch: steam on joins the thermostats' midpoint to neutral, bypassing the brew thermostat

F22.what: The 3-way valve's return, through the steam switch, so it only opens with steam off

F23.what: The steam switch's bypass of the brew thermostat

F24.what: Brew lamp lead: across the brew thermostat, so it lights once that opens

F25.what: Steam lamp lead: across the steam thermostat

F26.what: Steam thermostat to the brew thermostat

F27.what: Brew thermostat to the steam thermostat

F28.what: Steam lamp lead, on the elements' return

F29.what: The elements' return to the steam thermostat

F34.what: Pump feed, from the valve's spade, so brew runs the pump and opens the valve together

lampS.name: Steam lamp
lampS.note: Across the steam thermostat, so it lights once the boiler reaches steam temperature.

swS.name: Steam switch
swS.note: Steam off, it completes the 3-way valve's return to neutral. Steam on, it bypasses the brew thermostat, so the boiler heats to the steam thermostat's setting.

lampB.name: Brew lamp
lampB.note: Across the brew thermostat, so it lights once the boiler reaches brew temperature.

swB.name: Brew switch
swB.note: It joins line from after the thermal fuse (spade 4) to the 3-way valve's feed (spade 5), which also feeds the pump.

lampP.name: Power lamp
lampP.note: Between switched line and neutral, so it lights while the machine is on.

swP.name: Power switch
swP.note: It breaks both line (spades 4 and 5) and neutral (spades 1 and 2).

chassis.name: Chassis ground
chassis.note: Two earth spades on the frame.

cup.name: Cup warmer ground
cup.note: The cup warmer plate's earth spades.

boiler.name: Boiler
boiler.note: Two elements in parallel, with the 184 °C thermal fuse in series.

bt.name: Brew thermostat
bt.note: Out on every Gaggiuino install: the thermocouple goes in its hole, and the PCB takes over brew temperature.

st.name: Steam thermostat
st.note: On stock wiring it can stay, unplugged, or come out. On Plug-and-Play wiring the 185 °C resettable fuse goes in its hole.

sol.name: 3-way solenoid valve
sol.note: The 3-way solenoid valve. It opens while the brew switch is on with steam off.

sock.name: Power socket
sock.note: The IEC inlet: line, neutral and earth come in here.

pump.name: Pump and its 110 °C fuse
pump.note: The fuse's own lead plugs onto spade B (Pa, from its fuse). Its other lead runs to factory splice J0.

J0.name: Factory splice: neutral from the power switch, with the pump's return

J1.name: Factory splice: switched line from the power switch

J2.name: Factory splice: the neutral that feeds the power and brew lamps, the brew thermostat and the steam switch

J3.name: Factory splice: line after the 184 °C fuse

J4.name: Factory splice: between the two thermostats

J5.name: Factory splice: the elements' return to the steam thermostat

screen.note: Its cable plugs into J1. The screen's own pin names: GND, IO27, IO28, 5V on the Gen 3.5 (ESP32-P4); GND, IO18, IO17, 5V on the Gen 3 (ESP32-S3); GND, RX, TX, 5V on the headless board. J1's TX goes to the first of the middle two, its RX to the second.

l4b.name: L4b, left loose
l4b.note: Live whenever the machine is on. Its insulated spade stays on and it's tied back clear of everything.

screen.name: Screen
screen.note: Its cable plugs into J1. The screen's own pin names: GND, IO27, IO28, 5V on the Gen 3.5 (ESP32-P4); GND, IO18, IO17, 5V on the Gen 3 (ESP32-S3); GND, RX, TX, 5V on the headless board. J1's TX goes to the first of the middle two, its RX to the second.

F1.what: Line from the inlet to the power switch

F2.what: Neutral from the inlet to the 184 °C thermal fuse

F3.what: Neutral after the thermal fuse, to an element

F4.what: Neutral to the pump, through its 110 °C fuse: this end is connector F

F5.what: Neutral on from connector F to the 3-way valve

F6.what: Neutral on to the power switch's spade 8, a tie point (the power lamp sits between P and 8)

F8.what: Switched line to the steam switch

F9.what: Switched line to the brew switch's common

F10.what: Switched line on to the brew thermostat

F11.what: Steam on joins spade 3 to P(3-4), so line skips the brew thermostat

F12.what: Brew thermostat to the steam thermostat

F13.what: Heater line from the steam thermostat to the brew switch's spade 2, a tie point (the boiler lamp sits between P and 2)

F14.what: Heater line on to an element

F15.what: Heater line to the other element

F16.what: Brew switch output to the steam switch's second pole, P(5-6)

F18.what: The 3-way valve's feed, through the steam switch, so it only opens with steam off

lampB.name: Internal boiler lamp
lampB.note: Inside the switch housing, wired across brew P(1-2) and 2 (dotted on the drawing). It lights once the boiler is up to temperature.

housing.name: Switch housing
housing.note: Brew, steam and power rockers in one block, with the boiler lamp inside across brew P(1-2) and 2, and the power lamp across on/off P and 8.

lampP.name: Internal power lamp
lampP.note: Inside the switch housing, wired across on/off P and 8 (dotted on the drawing). It lights while the machine is on.

cup.name: Cup warmer ground
cup.note: The cup warmer plate's earth spades. Most 120 V Classics left the factory with no earth wire, so none lands here: the grounding retrofit adds one.

boiler.name: Boiler
boiler.note: Two elements in parallel, with the 184 °C thermal fuse in series.

bt.name: Brew thermostat
bt.note: Out on every Gaggiuino install: the thermocouple goes in its hole, and the PCB takes over brew temperature.

st.name: Steam thermostat
st.note: On stock wiring it can stay, unplugged, or come out. On Plug-and-Play wiring the 185 °C resettable fuse goes in its hole.

sol.name: 3-way solenoid valve
sol.note: The 3-way solenoid valve. It opens while the brew switch is on with steam off.

sock.name: Power socket
sock.note: The IEC inlet. Most 120 V Classics have a two-pole one with no earth pin, so only line and neutral come in.

pump.name: Pump and its 110 °C fuse
pump.note: The fuse's own lead plugs onto spade B (Pa, from its fuse). Its other lead ends in connector F, which joins two wires.

fac.name: Classic, 120 V, as it leaves the factory
fac.srcname: the official docs' 120 V Classic stock-integration drawing, whose thick lines are the stock wires apart from the install's purple ones and the retrofit's green earth
fac.noearth: Most 120 V Classics left the factory with no earth wire, so none is drawn. The drawing's green earth wires are the grounding retrofit.

l4b.name: L4b, left loose
l4b.note: Live whenever the machine is on. Its insulated spade stays on and it's tied back clear of everything.

screen.name: Screen
screen.note: Its cable plugs into J1. The screen's own pin names: GND, IO27, IO28, 5V on the Gen 3.5 (ESP32-P4); GND, IO18, IO17, 5V on the Gen 3 (ESP32-S3); GND, RX, TX, 5V on the headless board. J1's TX goes to the first of the middle two, its RX to the second.

F1.what: Line from the inlet to the power switch

F2.what: Neutral from the inlet to the 184 °C thermal fuse

F3.what: Earth from the inlet to the boiler

F4.what: Earth from the boiler to the cup warmer

F5.what: Neutral after the thermal fuse, to the elements

F6.what: Neutral to the pump: this end is connector F

F7.what: Link between the two elements: at 230 V they run in series

F8.what: Heater line from the steam thermostat to the elements

F9.what: Heater line to the brew switch's spade 2, for the boiler lamp, which sits between P and 2

F10.what: Steam on joins spade 3 to P(3-4), so line skips the brew thermostat

F11.what: Brew thermostat to the steam thermostat

F12.what: Switched line to the brew thermostat

F13.what: Switched line to the steam switch

F14.what: Switched line on to the brew switch's common

F15.what: Brew switch output to the steam switch's second pole, P(5-6)

F17.what: The 3-way valve's feed, through the steam switch, so it only opens with steam off

F18.what: Neutral for the power lamp, which sits between P and 8: it reaches spade 8 from the 3-way valve's spade

F19.what: Neutral from the 3-way valve to connector F on the pump

lampB.name: Internal boiler lamp
lampB.note: Inside the switch housing, wired across brew P(1-2) and 2 (dotted on the drawing). It lights once the boiler is up to temperature.

housing.name: Switch housing
housing.note: Brew, steam and power rockers in one block, with the boiler lamp inside across brew P(1-2) and 2, and the power lamp across on/off P and 8.

lampP.name: Internal power lamp
lampP.note: Inside the switch housing, wired across on/off P and 8 (dotted on the drawing). It lights while the machine is on.

cup.name: Cup warmer ground
cup.note: The cup warmer plate's earth spades.

boiler.name: Boiler
boiler.note: Two elements in series, linked TL to BL, with the 184 °C thermal fuse in series.

bt.name: Brew thermostat
bt.note: Out on every Gaggiuino install: the thermocouple goes in its hole, and the PCB takes over brew temperature.

st.name: Steam thermostat
st.note: On stock wiring it can stay, unplugged, or come out. On Plug-and-Play wiring the 185 °C resettable fuse goes in its hole.

sol.name: 3-way solenoid valve
sol.note: The 3-way solenoid valve. It opens while the brew switch is on with steam off.

sock.name: Power socket
sock.note: The IEC inlet: line, neutral and earth come in here.

pump.name: Pump (no fuse on this drawing)
pump.note: This drawing shows no pump fuse. Connector F, on spade B, joins two neutral wires.

fac.name: Classic, 230 V, as it leaves the factory
fac.srcname: the official docs' 220 to 240 V Classic stock-integration drawing, whose thick lines are the stock wires apart from the install's purple ones

screen.note: Its cable plugs into J1. The screen's own pin names: GND, IO27, IO28, 5V on the Gen 3.5 (ESP32-P4); GND, IO18, IO17, 5V on the Gen 3 (ESP32-S3); GND, RX, TX, 5V on the headless board. J1's TX goes to the first of the middle two, its RX to the second.

screen.name: Screen
screen.note: Its cable plugs into J1. The screen's own pin names: GND, IO27, IO28, 5V on the Gen 3.5 (ESP32-P4); GND, IO18, IO17, 5V on the Gen 3 (ESP32-S3); GND, RX, TX, 5V on the headless board. J1's TX goes to the first of the middle two, its RX to the second.

facnote.text: Out of the box isn't drawn for the 230 V Classic Pro: the official docs have no drawing of the plain 230 V Pro's stock wiring. Their archive has Gaggia's diagram of the 240 V Pro Eco, which adds a standby board.
